claims.sentence: On 30 September 2026 the WHO released a resource suite on preventing and managing heat-related illness at mass gatherings such as sporting and religious events.
claims.evidence: Release date 30 Sep 2026 and title supported by URL slug and summary; 'sporting and religious events' not found in retrieved WHO text, which says only 'mass gatherings'/'major events'.
claims.newSentence: On 30 September 2026 the WHO released a resource suite on preventing and managing heat-related illness at mass gatherings.

claims.sentence: The WHO released the guidance suite on 30 September 2026.
The WHO's evidence review of studies from 1980 to 2025 found nearly half a million medical encounters at mass gatherings, including more than 22,000 heat-related illnesses.
claims.evidence: 'covering studies published between 1980 and 2025 ... nearly half a million medical encounters ... more than 22,000 heat-related illnesses'.

claims.sentence: The suite includes a heat-risk assessment tool and is aimed at spectators, attendees, volunteers and workers as well as organisers.
claims.evidence: Heat-risk assessment tool is listed as a component. WHO page 'names spectators, attendees, volunteers and workers as those affected', not explicitly as the audience of the suite.
claims.newSentence: The suite includes a heat-risk assessment tool, and WHO names spectators, attendees, volunteers and workers among those affected by heat at mass gatherings.

claims.sentence: On 30 September 2026 the World Health Organization (WHO) released a resource suite called "Prevention and management of heat-related illness at mass gatherings".
claims.evidence: Title 'Prevention and management of heat-related illness at mass gatherings' and date 30 Sep 2026 match.

claims.sentence: The WHO says heat-related illness at major sporting, religious and cultural events has become a significant public health and operational risk.
claims.evidence: Retrieved text says heat-related illnesses at 'major events' are largely preventable or treatable; no statement found of 'significant public health and operational risk' or of sporting/religious/cultural events.
claims.newSentence: The WHO says most heat-related illnesses at major events can be prevented or treated on site when timely risk management measures are in place.

claims.sentence: Its evidence review of studies from 1980 to 2025 found nearly half a million medical encounters at mass gatherings, including more than 22,000 heat-related illnesses.
The guidance includes a heat-risk assessment tool and is intended to complement the WHO's heat-health action plan guidance and existing national plans.
claims.evidence: 'intended to complement WHO's heat-health action plan guidance, existing national heat-health action plans...'; heat-risk assessment tool listed as a component.

claims.sentence: The WHO urges governments, event organisers and partners to build heat risk management into health planning and event operations.
claims.evidence: 'calling on governments, event organizers and partners to integrate heat risk management into health planning, preparedness and operations'.

notes: Only search summaries of the WHO news item were retrieved, not full text. Examples 'sporting, religious and cultural' events appear nowhere in retrieved text (Tokyo 2020 and papal-visit items were third-party studies). Search noted some metadata date discrepancy on the release page; URL slug says 30-09-2026.
